original_question: Consider the nonlocal eigenvalue bounds sum_j |E_j|^{alpha} (delta(E_j) / |E_j|)^{beta} <= C_{alpha,beta,gamma,d} (hbar^{-d} int_{R^d} |V(x)|^{gamma + d/2} dx)^{alpha/gamma} for the eigenvalues E_j of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator -hbar^2 Delta + V with complex-valued potential V, where delta(E) := dist(E, [0, infinity)). In the six parameter regimes currently listed in the paper -- (a) alpha = 1/2, beta = 1, 0 < gamma < d/(2(2d-1)), d >= 2; (b) alpha > (d-1)gamma/(d/2-gamma), beta = 1, d/(2(2d-1)) <= gamma <= 1/2, d >= 2; (c) alpha = beta > 2gamma with gamma > 1/2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma <= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; (d) 0 < alpha < gamma(gamma + d/2), beta > 2gamma with gamma > 1/2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma >= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; (e) alpha = beta = gamma + d/2 with gamma >= 1/2 for d = 1 or gamma > 0 for d >= 2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma <= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; and (f) alpha > gamma, beta = gamma + d/2 with gamma >= 1/2 for d = 1 or gamma > 0 for d >= 2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma >= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2} -- for which values of d, alpha, beta, and gamma is this bound sharp up to a factor of hbar^{epsilon} for arbitrary epsilon > 0, and can the parameter region where such bounds hold be enlarged?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Question 3: the open problem asking for which of the six parameter regimes (a)–(f) the nonlocal Lieb–Thirring bound (9) is sharp up to a factor ħ^ε for every ε>0, and whether the parameter region for such bounds can be enlarged. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It identifies the correct nonlocal inequality (9), uses the right operator −ħ²Δ+V with the distance factor δ(E)=dist(E,[0,∞)), reproduces the six parameter regimes (a)–(f) essentially verbatim, and asks exactly the same two things as Question 3: sharpness up to ħ^ε and enlargement of the admissible parameter region. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works on the complex Hilbert space L²(R^d), with d≥1 an integer, and considers the semiclassical Schrödinger operator H_{ħ,V}=−ħ²Δ+V. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The E_j are the isolated eigenvalues of H_{ħ,V} lying outside [0,∞), each repeated according to algebraic multiplicity. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The standing hidden assumptions are that V is locally sufficiently regular and decays at infinity so that H_{ħ,V} can be defined as an m-sectorial operator and so that the spectrum outside [0,∞) is discrete; your draft omits these operator-theoretic hypotheses. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should say that the constant C_{α,β,γ,d} depends only on the parameters and not on V or ħ, and that one is asking for universal inequalities of type (9) for admissible complex potentials in the relevant L^{γ+d/2}(R^d) class. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

In cases (c)–(f), the sum is not over all discrete eigenvalues: it is restricted exactly to those j satisfying the stated truncation |E_j|^γ ≤ ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V|^{γ+d/2} or |E_j|^γ ≥ ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V|^{γ+d/2}. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The intended notion of sharpness is semiclassical sharpness as ħ→0; the surrounding discussion makes clear that the relevant quantity is the power of ħ, because that power measures the degree of locality violation. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The paper explicitly notes that the question is equivalent by scaling to the formulation with ħ=1; that equivalent form is implicit in your draft but not stated. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
refined_question: Let H_{ħ,V}=−ħ²Δ+V act in the complex Hilbert space L²(R^d), where d≥1 and V is a complex-valued potential for which H_{ħ,V} is m-sectorial and its spectrum in C outside [0,∞) consists of discrete eigenvalues E_j of finite algebraic multiplicity, repeated according to algebraic multiplicity; write δ(E)=dist(E,[0,∞)). For which parameter choices (d,α,β,γ) among the six regimes (a) α=1/2, β=1, 0<γ<d/(2(2d−1)), d≥2; (b) α>(d−1)γ/(d/2−γ), β=1, d/(2(2d−1))≤γ≤1/2, d≥2; (c) α=β>2γ, γ>1/2, with the sum restricted to eigenvalues satisfying |E_j|^γ≤ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx; (d) 0<α<γ(γ+d/2), β>2γ, γ>1/2, with the sum restricted to eigenvalues satisfying |E_j|^γ≥ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx; (e) α=β=γ+d/2, with γ≥1/2 if d=1 and γ>0 if d≥2, and with the sum restricted to eigenvalues satisfying |E_j|^γ≤ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx; and (f) α>γ, β=γ+d/2, with γ≥1/2 if d=1 and γ>0 if d≥2, and with the sum restricted to eigenvalues satisfying |E_j|^γ≥ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx, is the nonlocal Lieb–Thirring bound ∑_j |E_j|^α(δ(E_j)/|E_j|)^β ≤ C_{α,β,γ,d}(ħ^{−d}∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx)^{α/γ} sharp, up to a factor ħ^ε for every ε>0, in the semiclassical limit ħ→0? And can the parameter region for which bounds of this form are valid be enlarged? ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: By the scaling equivalence stated in the paper, this is equivalent to asking the same question with ħ=1: for which of the regimes (a)–(f) is ∑_j |E_j|^α(δ(E_j)/|E_j|)^β ≤ C_{α,β,γ,d}(∫_{R^d}|V(x)|^{γ+d/2}dx)^{α/γ}, with the same truncations in (c)–(f), sharp up to an arbitrarily small power loss, and can the admissible parameter region be enlarged? ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: your draft is essentially a long-form paraphrase of Section 2.2, Question 3, because it reproduces bound (9), the six admissible regimes (a)–(f), and the two precise tasks stated there. The only substantive omissions are the paper’s global operator/eigenvalue conventions from Section 1 and the surrounding Section 2 explanation that the sharpness issue is about the ħ→0 power law and the associated loss of locality. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
